To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed MLV-based pseudotype vectors that are CD4-specific and resistant to HIV-1 neutralization.
we have engineered MLV-derived retrovirus vectors pseudotyped with SIVagm Env proteins that selectively target CD4-expressin cells and are resistant to neutralization.

MLV capsid proteins, when complexed with SIVagm-derived envelope glycoprotein, form infectious pseudotype vectors that selectively transduce human CD4-exposing cells and are resistant to neutralization with antibodies against HIV-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of retroviral vectors for gene delivery into human cells.
the generation of novel retroviral vectors based on MLV, pseudotyped with the CD4-dependent Env proteins of HIV-1 and SIVagm, respectively.
the generation and characterization of novel MLV-derived retrovirus vectors that are suitable for gene transfer into CD+4 T-cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the [MLV(Sivagm)] pseudotyped vectors are resistant to the neutralization of HIV-specific antibodies in sera from AIDS patients.
the MLV vectors pseudotyped with SIVagm Env proteins are useful for the selective gene delivery to HIV-infected CD4+ T cells and for gene therapy of AIDS.
the MLV(SIVagM) pseudotyped vector is a promising candidate for the development of a vector system for the gene therapy of HIV-1 infection.
